command:
set +e
set -uo pipefail
export TMPDIR=/tmp HOME=/tmp MPLCONFIGDIR=/tmp/mpl MPLBACKEND=Agg
cd /tmp
# spawn runs task commands under bash -e; `set -uo pipefail` does not clear it (spawn#707).
echo "== staged bytes must match their pins =="
sha256sum -c pins.sha256 || { echo "FAIL: a staged check does not match its pin"; exit 1; }
mkdir -p wh && mv ./*.whl wh/ && (cd wh && sha256sum -c ../wheels.sha256) \
  || { echo "FAIL: a staged wheel does not match its pin"; exit 1; }

echo "== pytest from the staged wheels, offline (the env ships the tests but not pytest) =="
python3 -m pip install -q --no-index --find-links wh --no-deps wh/*.whl 2>&1 | grep -v "not on PATH" | tail -2
python3 -c "import pytest, xdist; print('pytest', pytest.__version__, ' pytest-xdist', xdist.__version__)" \
  || { echo "FAIL: pytest did not install from the staged wheels"; exit 1; }
python3 - > show.txt 2>&1 <<'VEOF'
import importlib
try:
    from threadpoolctl import threadpool_info
    for p in threadpool_info():
        print("threadpool", p.get("internal_api"), p.get("num_threads"), p.get("architecture", ""))
except Exception as exc:
    print("threadpool unavailable (%s)" % type(exc).__name__)
for m in ("nilearn", "nibabel", "numpy", "scipy", "sklearn", "pandas", "polars", "pyarrow", "numpydoc", "pytest", "xdist", "pytest_timeout", "pytest_rerunfailures"):
    try:
        print(m, getattr(importlib.import_module(m), "__version__", "unknown"))
    except Exception as exc:
        print(m, "unavailable (%s)" % type(exc).__name__)
VEOF
cat show.txt

echo "== Nilearn's own suite, the three groups its tox.ini runs (testenv:latest + testenv:flaky) =="
# Some tests write beside themselves (test_as_ndarray_memmap writes _utils/tests/data/mmap.dat).
# Nilearn's CI runs from a writable checkout; the installed package is read-only to the
# container user. So run a copy in /tmp -- and prove it is the same bytes first.
SRC=$(python3 -c "import nilearn, os; print(os.path.dirname(nilearn.__file__))")
mkdir -p /tmp/pkg && cp -r "$SRC" /tmp/pkg/nilearn && diff -r -q "$SRC" /tmp/pkg/nilearn \
  || { echo "FAIL: the writable copy of nilearn differs from the installed package"; exit 1; }
export PYTHONPATH=/tmp/pkg:/tmp
python3 -c "import nilearn; assert nilearn.__file__.startswith('/tmp/pkg/'), nilearn.__file__; print('testing', nilearn.__file__, '(byte-identical copy of', '$SRC)')" \
  || { echo "FAIL: the suite would not import the copy"; exit 1; }
N=$(nproc)
# pytest-xdist aborts with "Different tests were collected between gw0 and gw1" when a
# parametrization iterates a set: each worker hashes strings with its own seed. A fixed seed is
# xdist's documented remedy; it changes iteration order, not what any test asserts.
export PYTHONHASHSEED=0
P="--pyargs nilearn -p no:cacheprovider -p order -p account"
W="-W error::sklearn.exceptions.ConvergenceWarning -W error::FutureWarning"
ACCOUNT_OUT=collect-all.json python3 -m pytest $P --collect-only -q > collect-all.log 2>&1
run_group() {   # name, marker expression, extra args
  ACCOUNT_OUT=collect-$1.json python3 -m pytest $P -m "$2" --collect-only -q > collect-$1.log 2>&1
  T0=$(date +%s)
  # Under xdist, each worker gets ONE OpenMP/OpenBLAS thread. Every worker otherwise brings a
  # pool as wide as the box, and oversubscribed libgomp threads busy-wait against each other:
  # measured, a check_img_estimator_dtypes test that takes 13 s alone took 3,824 s in a
  # 16-worker run. Alone, one thread is no slower (199 s vs 206 s for six of them), which is
  # why the serial group keeps the default.
  case "$3" in *"-n "*) TH="OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1" ;; *) TH="" ;; esac
  env $TH ACCOUNT_OUT=run-$1.json python3 -u -m pytest $P -m "$2" $3 -q -rfEs > suite-$1.log 2>&1
  echo "$? $(( $(date +%s) - T0 ))s" > rc-$1; echo "group $1: exit/wall $(cat rc-$1)"
  # to stdout too, so a run killed later still leaves this group's verdict in command.log
  grep -E "^(FAILED|ERROR)|^=+ .*(passed|failed|error)" suite-$1.log | tail -25
}
# serial before slow: the slow group is the long one, so the serial verdict should not depend on it
run_group fast   "not slow and not flaky and not single_process" "$W --timeout=60 -n $N"
run_group serial "flaky or single_process"                       ""
run_group slow   "slow and not flaky and not single_process"     "$W -n $N --durations=40"
sed -n '/slowest .* durations/,/^=/p' suite-slow.log | head -45
python3 -u suite_check.py fast slow serial 2>&1 | tee suite-summary.txt
test "${PIPESTATUS[0]}" = "0" || { echo "FAIL: Nilearn's own suite did not pass cleanly"; for g in fast slow serial; do tail -30 suite-$g.log; done; exit 1; }

echo "== four APIs against closed forms =="
python3 -u identities.py 2>&1 | tee identities.log
test "${PIPESTATUS[0]}" = "0" || { echo "FAIL: an identity failed"; exit 1; }
grep -q 'NILEARN IDENTITIES OK' identities.log || { echo "FAIL: no completion sentinel"; exit 1; }
uname -m | awk '{print "arch\t"$1}'
echo "DONE"
